pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.body: Both writes store retryCount=1, so a reminder that failed twice never exceeds the `gt: 1` deletion threshold and keeps being re-processed by every cron run, defeating the purpose of the retry cap.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Lost update under concurrent cron executions leaves the retry counter permanently below the delete threshold.
raw_findings.impact: Both writes store retryCount=1, so a reminder that failed twice never exceeds the `gt: 1` deletion threshold and keeps being re-processed by every cron run, defeating the purpose of the retry cap.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new increment logic derives the new counter value from a value read earlier in the request rather than letting the database perform the increment atomically.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic update, e.g. `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, at both increment sites instead of computing the new value from the stale in-memory `reminder.retryCount`.
raw_findings.title: retryCount incremented via non-atomic read-modify-write
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping executions of the scheduleSMSReminders cron (or a retry of the same cron invocation) both read the same reminder row with retryCount=0 and both write 0+1.

raw_findings.body: The exception thrown from inside the catch block is not handled, so the for-loop terminates, all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are never processed, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the `SMS scheduled` response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Secondary exception escapes the loop and aborts processing of all subsequent reminders in the cron run.
raw_findings.impact: The exception thrown from inside the catch block is not handled, so the for-loop terminates, all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are never processed, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the `SMS scheduled` response.
raw_findings.root_cause: An awaited DB write was added to the error-handling path without any error handling of its own.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (logging failures) or use `updateMany({ where: { id: reminder.id } })` so a missing row does not throw.
raw_findings.title: Unguarded prisma.update inside catch can abort the whole reminder loop
raw_findings.trigger: The caught error is itself a database/connection failure, or the reminder row was concurrently deleted (e.g. by deleteScheduledSMSReminder from a booking cancellation) between the findMany and this update, causing Prisma to throw P2025 "record not found".

raw_findings.body: The SMS cron deletes reminders belonging to other delivery methods, silently dropping email/WhatsApp reminders that this endpoint has no ownership over.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Over-broad delete predicate removes rows outside the handler's intended scope.
raw_findings.impact: The SMS cron deletes reminders belonging to other delivery methods, silently dropping email/WhatsApp reminders that this endpoint has no ownership over.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new OR branch filters solely on the shared retryCount column without repeating the method constraint that scopes this handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR branch so the retry-based deletion only affects SMS reminders.
raw_findings.title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
raw_findings.trigger: Any WorkflowReminder row of another method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) having retryCount > 1 — e.g. as soon as the WhatsApp or email schedulers start incrementing the shared retryCount column.

raw_findings.body: retryCount reaches 2 and the next cron run's deleteMany permanently removes the reminder, so a valid reminder is never sent even though the underlying condition (rate window, outage) resolved before the scheduled date.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate reminders are irrecoverably deleted after two transient errors.
raw_findings.impact: retryCount reaches 2 and the next cron run's deleteMany permanently removes the reminder, so a valid reminder is never sent even though the underlying condition (rate window, outage) resolved before the scheduled date.
raw_findings.root_cause: The catch block treats every thrown error, including transient ones, as a countable scheduling failure.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only increment retryCount for permanent/validation errors (e.g. inspect the Twilio error code) or leave rate-limit/transport errors without incrementing, so transient failures do not consume the retry budget.
raw_findings.title: Transient failures (SMS rate limit, Twilio outage) cause permanent reminder deletion
raw_findings.trigger: `twilio.scheduleSMS` throws for a non-permanent reason, e.g. `checkSMSRateLimit` throwing when a user hits the monthly SMS limit, or a temporary Twilio/network error, on two consecutive cron runs.

raw_findings.body: retryCount reaches 2 and the reminders of that team/user are deleted by the next run, so after an admin unlocks SMS sending the pending reminders no longer exist and are never delivered.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Administrative lock state silently causes permanent deletion of pending reminders.
raw_findings.impact: retryCount reaches 2 and the reminders of that team/user are deleted by the next run, so after an admin unlocks SMS sending the pending reminders no longer exist and are never delivered.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new else-branch equates a deliberate no-op return from scheduleSMS with a delivery failure.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish the locked case from a genuine scheduling failure (e.g. have scheduleSMS signal the lock, or skip incrementing when the user/team is locked) instead of treating any falsy return as a retryable failure.
raw_findings.title: SMS-lock path (undefined return) counted as a scheduling failure
raw_findings.trigger: A team or user is in SMSLockState.LOCKED, so `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` without any error; two cron runs occur while the lock is in place.

raw_findings.body: The enclosing `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` guard is false, so no increment occurs and the reminder is re-selected by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the endless re-scheduling this PR intends to stop.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incomplete coverage of failure paths keeps the reported endless-retry behavior for a subset of reminders.
raw_findings.impact: The enclosing `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` guard is false, so no increment occurs and the reminder is re-selected by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the endless re-scheduling this PR intends to stop.
raw_findings.root_cause: The retry accounting was only added to the two paths inside the message/sendTo guard, leaving the guard-false path unbounded.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Also increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) in an else branch of the `if (message?.length ... && sendTo)` guard so unsendable reminders are bounded too.
raw_findings.title: No retryCount increment when sendTo or message is missing
raw_findings.trigger: A reminder whose workflow step has no sendTo and whose booking has no smsReminderNumber, or whose rendered message is empty, is picked up by the cron.

raw_findings.body: The comment understates the query: it also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, so maintainers can misjudge which rows this cron removes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale documentation misleads future maintainers about the deletion criteria.
raw_findings.impact: The comment understates the query: it also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, so maintainers can misjudge which rows this cron removes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The delete predicate was extended with a retryCount branch without updating the describing comment.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the preceding comment to state that reminders past their scheduled date OR with more than one failed scheduling attempt are deleted.
raw_findings.title: Comment above deleteMany no longer describes the new retry-based deletion
raw_findings.trigger: A reader inspecting scheduleSMSReminders.ts sees the unchanged comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" directly above the now two-branch delete.

raw_findings.body: The OR branch on the unindexed retryCount column forces a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on each cron run, increasing query latency and DB load.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Hot cron query degrades to a full-table scan as the reminder table grows.
raw_findings.impact: The OR branch on the unindexed retryCount column forces a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on each cron run, increasing query latency and DB load.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new filter predicate was introduced on a freshly added column without a corresponding index.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either add an index covering retryCount (e.g. @@index([method, retryCount])) in schema.prisma plus a migration, or scope the branch so it can use the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index.
raw_findings.title: retryCount filter has no supporting index on WorkflowReminder
raw_findings.trigger: Every cron invocation runs this deleteMany on a large WorkflowReminder table; the existing indexes cover (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) and (cancelled, scheduledDate) but nothing on retryCount.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the retry accounting (e.g. never reaching the `gt: 1` threshold, or deleting reminders on the first failure) ship undetected, since the only behavior change of this PR is untested.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Behavioral regressions in the retry cap are not caught by CI.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the retry accounting (e.g. never reaching the `gt: 1` threshold, or deleting reminders on the first failure) ship undetected, since the only behavior change of this PR is untested.
raw_findings.root_cause: New retry/deletion logic was added without accompanying test coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test for the scheduleSMSReminders handler that mocks twilio.scheduleSMS to fail/return undefined and asserts retryCount is incremented and that reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the following run.
raw_findings.title: No test covers retryCount increment and retry-based deletion
raw_findings.trigger: Running the repository test suite after this change; no test exercises the SMS cron handler with a failing twilio.scheduleSMS.

validated_findings.failure_mode: Administrative lock state silently causes permanent deletion of pending reminders.
validated_findings.impact: retryCount reaches 2 and the reminders of that team/user are deleted by the next run, so after an admin unlocks SMS sending the pending reminders no longer exist and are never delivered.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new else-branch equates a deliberate no-op return from scheduleSMS with a delivery failure.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish the locked case from a genuine scheduling failure (e.g. have scheduleSMS signal the lock, or skip incrementing when the user/team is locked) instead of treating any falsy return as a retryable failure.
validated_findings.title: SMS-lock path (undefined return) counted as a scheduling failure
validated_findings.trigger: A team or user is in SMSLockState.LOCKED, so `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` without any error; two cron runs occur while the lock is in place.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that SMS lock returns undefined and counts as failure is plausible but speculative. twilioProvider.scheduleSMS returns undefined when locked, but this is intentional no-op behavior. Whether this should increment retryCount is a design decision, not a clear bug.

validated_findings.body: The enclosing `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` guard is false, so no increment occurs and the reminder is re-selected by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the endless re-scheduling this PR intends to stop.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Incomplete coverage of failure paths keeps the reported endless-retry behavior for a subset of reminders.
validated_findings.impact: The enclosing `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` guard is false, so no increment occurs and the reminder is re-selected by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the endless re-scheduling this PR intends to stop.
validated_findings.root_cause: The retry accounting was only added to the two paths inside the message/sendTo guard, leaving the guard-false path unbounded.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Also increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) in an else branch of the `if (message?.length ... && sendTo)` guard so unsendable reminders are bounded too.
validated_findings.title: No retryCount increment when sendTo or message is missing
validated_findings.trigger: A reminder whose workflow step has no sendTo and whose booking has no smsReminderNumber, or whose rendered message is empty, is picked up by the cron.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that missing sendTo/message causes endless retry is speculative. Looking at the code, if the guard is false, the reminder simply isn't processed this run. The PR's goal is to cap retries for scheduling failures, not for validation failures. This is a design gap, not a proven defect.

validated_findings.body: The comment understates the query: it also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, so maintainers can misjudge which rows this cron removes.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale documentation misleads future maintainers about the deletion criteria.
validated_findings.impact: The comment understates the query: it also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, so maintainers can misjudge which rows this cron removes.
validated_findings.root_cause: The delete predicate was extended with a retryCount branch without updating the describing comment.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the preceding comment to state that reminders past their scheduled date OR with more than one failed scheduling attempt are deleted.
validated_findings.title: Comment above deleteMany no longer describes the new retry-based deletion
validated_findings.trigger: A reader inspecting scheduleSMSReminders.ts sees the unchanged comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" directly above the now two-branch delete.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a documentation/comment issue, not a functional defect. The comment at line 28 is stale but does not cause runtime misbehavior. Stylistic/doc issues are excluded per instructions.

validated_findings.body: The OR branch on the unindexed retryCount column forces a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on each cron run, increasing query latency and DB load.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Hot cron query degrades to a full-table scan as the reminder table grows.
validated_findings.impact: The OR branch on the unindexed retryCount column forces a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on each cron run, increasing query latency and DB load.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new filter predicate was introduced on a freshly added column without a corresponding index.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either add an index covering retryCount (e.g. @@index([method, retryCount])) in schema.prisma plus a migration, or scope the branch so it can use the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index.
validated_findings.title: retryCount filter has no supporting index on WorkflowReminder
validated_findings.trigger: Every cron invocation runs this deleteMany on a large WorkflowReminder table; the existing indexes cover (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) and (cancelled, scheduledDate) but nothing on retryCount.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing index is speculative. No evidence that retryCount lacks an index or that this causes performance issues. The schema shows existing indexes but absence of proof of a problem is not proof of a defect.

validated_findings.body: Regressions in the retry accounting (e.g. never reaching the `gt: 1` threshold, or deleting reminders on the first failure) ship undetected, since the only behavior change of this PR is untested.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Behavioral regressions in the retry cap are not caught by CI.
validated_findings.impact: Regressions in the retry accounting (e.g. never reaching the `gt: 1` threshold, or deleting reminders on the first failure) ship undetected, since the only behavior change of this PR is untested.
validated_findings.root_cause: New retry/deletion logic was added without accompanying test coverage.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test for the scheduleSMSReminders handler that mocks twilio.scheduleSMS to fail/return undefined and asserts retryCount is incremented and that reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the following run.
validated_findings.title: No test covers retryCount increment and retry-based deletion
validated_findings.trigger: Running the repository test suite after this change; no test exercises the SMS cron handler with a failing twilio.scheduleSMS.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap findings are excluded as they describe missing coverage rather than a concrete defect introduced by the patch.
